narratives.Overview:
- relieves: P1 — Add Taskfile task swarm:finalize-owed that invokes engine verb swarm-finalize-owed with the same :engine:invoke shape as finalize-cohort.
- relieves: P1 — Add a test that every backtick task <name> in evaluateFinalizeOwedSessionGate live-inventory and probe remedy lines plus FINALIZE_OWED_USAGE resolves in the Taskfile include graph.
- relieves: P1 — On the repo-required gate branch, drop only the task swarm:finalize-owed half of the remedy line and keep pass --defer-owed <reason>.
- relieves: P1 — Accept --defer-owed <non-empty reason> on session:ready parseArgs and thread it into sessionStartOptions.deferOwedReason for the runSessionStart re-run path without changing same-root inheritDeferOwedFromPrimary semantics.
- relieves: P2 — Extend remoteClaimMeta to return the resolved claim sha or null, resolve the fetched private-ref OID for proof, and refuse landed classification when sha is null or git proof reads fail.
- relieves: P2 — Share one landed-claim proof helper on both completed-brief and nonterminal stale+failed-issue-read branches: tip-ancestor OR non-empty claim-vs-merge-base changed paths whose tip entries match presence, mode/type, and OID (treat both-absent only as verified absence).
- relieves: P2 — Classify landed-leftover blocks false only after that shared proof succeeds; otherwise keep stale-unverified blocks true; keep verified-open stale/close-owed unchanged; accept measured residual still-blocking claims such as pr-5259 under byte/mode inequality.
- relieves: P2 — Add landed-leftover to FinalizeOwedState and ensure a completed-loop landed-leftover classification is not suppressed by a nonterminal stale-unverified twin, with a fixture that uses null briefPairingKey so tipHasTwin does not divert first.
- relieves: P2 — State empty changed-path sets as absence of B-proof and cover completed divergent claim, unavailable claim object, squash-equivalent claim, marker-empty-diff still-blocking, residual alias-divergent still-blocking (pr-5259 class), and null-pairing twin fixtures.
- relieves: P3 — Include story.detail for unverified, stale-unverified, and landed-leftover rows in formatFinalizeOwedInventoryLines, add an inventory channel for aggregated issue-read failure printable when the row list is empty, and emit a landed-leftover warning on the finalizeOwed CLI path.
- relieves: P3 — Under total issue-read failure, print class-specific aggregated remedies that distinguish missing-credential auth from HTTP 410, rate-limit via detectRateLimit/RATE_LIMIT_RE, and missing-binary, never reuse isTransientClaimFetchFailure alone as the auth discriminator, and clear the gate only when every stale+failed-read row carries positive local-git landed proof while residual unproven stale+failed-read rows keep blocking via --defer-owed and pre-existing non-stale unverified blocks:false rows stay non-blocking.
- relieves: P4 — When resolveBinaryForArgv throws in defaultRunGh, return returncode -1 with the ScmStubError text immediately and preserve ghx-to-gh spawn fallback only after a binary was resolved and a spawn was attempted.
narratives.UserStory: As a maintainer, I want finalize-owed remedies and landed-claim proof, so that Prefer-A Bound product work can ship without activation/write-fence blocks.

## In plain English

Session start can freeze you with a finalize-owed message that names a task and a flag that do not work. Leftover finalize claim branches for already-closed issues also block whenever GitHub issue reads fail, and nothing supported clears them. This Prefer-A makes the printed remedy real, lets session:ready take the same defer flag, stops landed closed leftovers from blocking on read failure alone, adds a dry-runnable prune for proven landed closed claims, and surfaces why issue reads failed (including missing gh) without throwing.

## Bound remedy

- relieves: P1 — Add Taskfile task swarm:finalize-owed that invokes engine verb swarm-finalize-owed with the same :engine:invoke shape as finalize-cohort.
- relieves: P1 — Add a test that every task <name> string in evaluateFinalizeOwedSessionGate remedy lines and FINALIZE_OWED_USAGE resolves in the Taskfile include graph.

## What happens

At master `88be44b04`, a mutation `session:start` or `session:ready` can refuse with:

```
finalize owed blocks mutation: run `task swarm:finalize-owed` or pass --defer-owed <reason>
```

Following that remedy does not work. The inventory behind it can also block when nothing is actually owed.

## Problems

### 1. The remedy names a task that doesn't exist, and suggests a flag the failing verb rejects

- `evaluateFinalizeOwedSessionGate` (`packages/core/src/session/session-start.ts`) pushes that line in three branches: the injected-probe path, the "repo required" path, and the live inventory path. `FINALIZE_OWED_USAGE` (`packages/core/src/swarm/finalize-owed-cli.ts`) also says `Usage: task swarm:finalize-owed`.
- No Taskfile defines `swarm:finalize-owed`. `tasks/swarm.yml` has `readiness`, `pre-dispatch`, `launch`, `routing-set`, `verify-review-clean`, `complete-cohort` and `finalize-cohort`, and no other `tasks/*.yml` or `Taskfile.yml` mentions it.
- The command exists only as the engine verb `swarm-finalize-owed`, in `CORE_MODULE_VERBS` and the `case "swarm-finalize-owed"` branch of `packages/runtime/src/dispatch.ts`. `engine:invoke` is `internal: true`, so an operator can't reach the verb through `task`.
- `task session:ready` doesn't accept `--defer-owed`. `parseArgs` in `packages/runtime/src/session-ready.ts` accepts only `--project-root`, `--repo`, `--session-id`, `--with-network` and `--json`, and returns `unrecognized argument: --defer-owed` with exit 2. Only `session:start` parses `--defer-owed` (`packages/runtime/src/session-start.ts`).
- `runSessionReady` (`packages/core/src/session/session-ready.ts`) re-runs `runSessionStart` with `options.sessionStartOptions` whenever the quick-tier inspect fails, the bound session id differs, or a steal is requested. No defer reason is carried into that call. So a `session:start --defer-owed` from earlier doesn't help once the ritual is stale or bound to a different session id. `session:ready` then hits the gate again, and the operator is told to pass a flag that `session:ready` refuses.
  - The one exception is a linked worktree that inherits from a fresh primary ritual (`inheritDeferOwedFromPrimary`).

### 2. Leftover `swarm/finalize/pr-*` branches whose issues are closed block whenever issue reads fail, and nothing supported clears them

In `discoverFinalizeOwed` (`packages/core/src/swarm/finalize-owed.ts`), the loop over completed briefs runs these checks in order:
1. `listOpenFinalizePrs`
2. `remoteClaimMeta`
3. `fetchIssueState`

When the claim ref exists and is older than `FINALIZE_CLAIM_STALE_MS` (2 h), and the issue GET fails, the row becomes `stale-unverified` with `blocks: true`. The issue-closed skip (`issueState.state === "closed"`) is never reached.

At `88be44b04`:
- origin has 17 `swarm/finalize/*` branches. They are leftover-complete heads from earlier cohorts, roughly three to nine weeks old.
- 15 of them equal `finalizeClaimRef(null, [productPullRequest], [issue])` for a completed brief.
- Every one of those 15 origin issues is closed.

So any session whose issue reads fail reports 15 blocking rows, even though nothing is owed.

When issue reads succeed, the same tip inventories to 0 owed, 0 close-owed and 0 stale. It has 11 non-blocking `unverified` rows: unmarked active briefs, plus one origin issue that returns HTTP 410.

`finalizeOwed` can't clear these rows:
- `stale-unverified` is skipped with the warning `origin-issue unverified; claim still blocking` and the run exits `EXIT_INCOMPLETE` (3).
- `deleteStaleClaim` runs only for `stale`, and `stale` requires a successful read showing the issue open.
- For closed issues the code intentionally never reclaims or deletes ("Closed origin: do not reclaim/delete a finalize branch for finished work").
- A leftover head that has already merged therefore stays a latent blocker forever. The only ways out are `--defer-owed` or deleting branches by hand.

`formatFinalizeOwedInventoryLines` prints `#N <state> [blocks] pr=#P <relPath>` and drops `detail`. So the operator never sees why the read failed (auth, 410, rate limit, missing binary).

### 3. Issue reads need an authenticated GitHub CLI; the public repo isn't read anonymously

This is what the code shows:
- Every GitHub read in the inventory goes through `defaultRunGh` (`packages/core/src/pr-protected-issues/gh.ts`), which runs the `gh` (or `ghx`) binary with `execFileSync` (no shell) and inherits the process environment. The reads are:
  - `fetchIssueState`: `gh api repos/{o}/{r}/issues/{n}`
  - `listOpenFinalizePrs`: `gh api repos/{o}/{r}/pulls?state=open&per_page=100`
  - `snapshotAccepts`: `gh api repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}`
- The session gate calls `discoverFinalizeOwed` with no injected `runGh`, so it uses `defaultRunGh`.
- `classifyScmArgv` (`packages/core/src/scm/call-shape.ts`) labels these single-positional `gh api` calls `cached-get`. `resolveBinaryForRole` then uses `resolveBinary` (`packages/core/src/scm/binary.ts`), which tries `ghx` first and then `gh`.
- `ghxSpawnFallbackBinary` (`packages/core/src/scm/spawn-status.ts`) retries with `gh` only after a `ghx` availability-class spawn failure, not after an HTTP or auth error.
- No path in this inventory reads anonymously over REST, and there is no other fallback. A non-zero `gh` exit becomes `fetchIssueState.error`, which leads to `unverified` or `stale-unverified`.
- `resolveBinaryForArgv` is called **outside** the `try` in `defaultRunGh`. If neither `ghx` nor `gh` is on PATH, `ScmStubError` is thrown, not returned as an error result. I haven't traced how `session:start` handles that throw. **Unconfirmed.**
- Separately, the git side (`fetchDeliveryTipPrivate`, `remoteClaimMeta`'s `ls-remote` and fetch) uses plain `git` and works anonymously against a public repo. So the tip and claim refs resolve while every issue read fails, which is exactly how problem 2 arises.

What the code doesn't show:
- That `gh api` with no `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` and no `gh auth login` refuses to make the request. That is GitHub CLI behaviour outside this repo. I believe it holds but haven't verified it in an isolated environment. **Unconfirmed.**
- Whether `ghx`, if installed, serves these paths from cache without credentials. **Unconfirmed.**

## Proposed

1. Add a `swarm:finalize-owed` task to `tasks/swarm.yml` (via `:engine:invoke` with `ENGINE_CMD: 'swarm-finalize-owed {{.CLI_ARGS}} --project-root "{{.USER_WORKING_DIR}}"'`, the same shape as `finalize-cohort`), or change every remedy and usage string to a command that actually runs. Add a test asserting that each `task <name>` named in a session remedy string exists in the Taskfile graph.
2. Make the remedy verb-aware. Either:
   - accept `--defer-owed <reason>` on `session:ready` and pass it into `sessionStartOptions` (recorded in ritual state as it is for `session:start`); or
   - when the refusal comes from `session:ready`, print `task session:start -- --defer-owed <reason>` followed by `task session:ready`, and make sure ready doesn't drop a recorded, unexpired defer when it re-runs start.
   - In both cases, `--defer-owed` is accepted only as a CLI flag with a non-empty reason, never from an environment variable or config. It is printed in the session output, recorded in ritual state, and scoped to the current worktree's ritual. A defer recorded in a primary checkout is shown as inherited when a linked worktree uses it.
3. Don't let a closed-origin leftover claim block because a read failed:
   - Before `stale-unverified`, check whether the claim head is already an ancestor of the delivery tip. If so, classify the row as non-blocking (for example `landed-leftover`). This check uses local git only; it is the only way a row becomes non-blocking without a successful issue read.
   - Add a supported prune: `swarm-finalize-owed --prune-landed-claims [--dry-run]`. It deletes only `swarm/finalize/*` branches whose head is reachable from the delivery tip and whose origin issue is verified closed. It prints the list in dry-run and refuses when verification fails.
4. Make read failures visible and recoverable:
   - Print `detail` for `unverified` and `stale-unverified` rows in `formatFinalizeOwedInventoryLines`, or at least one aggregated `issue reads failed: <reason>` line.
   - When issue reads can't be verified (for example every read fails with an auth-class error), the gate still refuses (fail closed), but with one specific remedy that names the missing credential and the failure reason, instead of N undifferentiated blocking rows. Only rows proven landed from local git alone (item 3) become non-blocking without a successful read.
   - Optionally, add an anonymous REST GET path for the three read shapes as a way to verify without a credential. Use it only after confirming the repo is public, never send a token on it, stay within the anonymous rate limit, and say when it was used.
5. Move `resolveBinaryForArgv` inside the `try` in `defaultRunGh` so a missing binary returns `returncode: -1` with the ScmStubError text instead of throwing.
